notes: Plans: Pls. iii, iv, vi, xvii, xxiii, xxxix carry only a local excavation grid (A-F, 1-5; one square = 20 m, from the Pl. iii scale bar); none gives national-grid coordinates, so the unit point (193650/127650) cannot be placed and no plan position is used. Positions are from the text: from the site ('of the ruins', 'of Khirbet Qumran', 'north-western entrance', 'south-eastern quarter') = unit; from a building, courtyard, cistern or the wadi = other. TYPE DECISION: p. 9 says 'The cisterns were uncovered' (open). Following PROTOCOL 3 ('A cistern is a pit') every feature the source calls a cistern is coded pit; loc. 91, which the source also calls 'a reservoir' (pp. 43, 131), is coded pool. An analyst who reads open cisterns as pools would change f1-f3, f10, f12, f13, f16, f17. GRAVE TYPE: main-cemetery tombs (and the north cemetery, 'similar') are a 1.2-2 m dug shaft with a loculus cut sideways at the bottom and sealed; coded cavity_with_opening true as shaft-and-loculus tombs. The source does not use the word 'shaft'; a reader could code them as pit graves (false). This bears on the C2 tomb-shaft variant through f23 (N). Merged/not coded: 'a cistern, loc. 66' (p. 4) whose steps overlie the kilns appears to be cistern 48/49 (p. 7 says the same of 48), so not coded twice; aqueduct and channels; the natural rock basin at the aqueduct head and the natural 'pools of Wadi Qumran' (p. 85), not built or rock-cut and not located; the clay-levigation basin 75 (a workshop vat); the stone basin of washing-place 52; the small wall basin in loc. 4; the Period III defensive ditch; the pots of animal bones (not burials). No mouth relation is stated. No explicit absence statement.
